EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Dealer Selling Nice Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat, Muscle Car Costs a Lot Less Than a New Charger
20 photos
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions
Can we interest you in a Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat ? You probably said yes. After all, you are now here, reading these lines and looking to find out whether the example pictured below is worth your time, and, better said, your hard-earned money.
If you are indeed in the market for such a model, then you know that these are on the affordable side of things today. That is if you aim for an older model year, as these tend to go for roughly 40,000 in today’s market. Sure, paying that sum would get you a high-mileage example, most of the time, whereas for roughly $15,000 to $20,000 more, you’d get a later model year car with fewer miles, whereas $75,000 or so would get you a barely driven example that’s much newer.
On a six-digit budget, the superior Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 becomes available, as this one now sells for between $100,000 and close to $150,000. And as a quick reminder, it remains the fastest and most powerful production muscle car ever. Beat that Ford and Chevrolet! And Dodge, too, for that matter. No, seriously, Dodge, please beat that, because the automotive world needs another neck-snappingly fast muscle car, and you’re the undisputed king when it comes to these!
Photo: Instagram | automotive_ambitions Mind you, we are not here to talk about a possible spiritual successor to the mighty Demon 170, nor to remind you that Ford is still the only company that offers V8-powered muscle cars, nor to refresh your memory about the fact that the Chevrolet Camaro is dead. For now, anyway. Instead, we should put the spotlight on the vehicle pictured in the gallery, which, as mentioned above, is looking for a new home, and it is a US-registered car, with a clean title.
According to the listing, the ride in question is a 2016 model year Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat , presented in white with golden wheels, red brake calipers, plenty of black details, and tinted windows. It features a red and black interior, remote engine start, a power sunroof, Laguna Performance Seats, and a few other things that are mentioned in the ad. As for the odometer, it read 57,000 miles (~91,700 km) or so at the time of cataloging.
Power is supplied by none other than the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 Hellcat lump. The unit was good for 707 hp (717 ps/527 kW) and 650 lb-ft (881 Nm) of torque when the car was new, and everything goes to the rear axle via an eight-speed automatic transmission. From 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph), this model needed a little over three and a half seconds, and the top speed was 199 mph (320 kph).
As for the how much it costs part of the story, you are looking at $43,991. That’s less than a new Charger, as mentioned in the title, which has an MSRP of $49,995. View this post on Instagram A post shared by AUTOMOTIVE AMBITIONS (@automotive_ambitions)
